text:
Alex: Heads-up — ran an nsys trace on the KV prefetch + batching path. Timeline shows repeated device-idle spikes even though kernels are queued.
Priya: Can you paste the nsys command you used and a short timeline snippet? :thinking:
Alex: Command I used:\n```\nnsys profile -o out_kvprefetch --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --capture-range=cudaAPI --force-overwrite --sample=none --stats true --stop-on-range-end yes --unified-memory=none -- \n  ./run_inference --profile-kv\n```\nScreenshot: big gaps between host submits (~20-30ms) then a burst of kernels. Copy engine (DMA) shows memcpy bursts but kernels don't overlap well.
Sam: That screams CPU-side submission gaps. Are we doing synchronous host copies or blocking syncs in the batching loop?
Alex: Our prefetch loop does something like:\n```\nfor batch in batches:\n    prefetch_hostbuf(batch)   # returns host pointer\n    cudaMemcpy(h2d, hostbuf, sz, cudaMemcpyDefault); // sync in our runtime\n    launch_kernel(stream_compute, ...);\n```\nWe relied on the runtime's heuristic to async-optimize but looks like it falls back to sync memcpy for large pages.
Priya: If cudaMemcpy is called (not cudaMemcpyAsync) we force the copy to complete before launch -> host thread won't submit kernels until after copy. And the Python GIL/GC could add additional jitter.
Jonah: Also check if the memcpy uses pageable memory. If it's pageable, host->device will be synchronous and use staging which stalls CPU and copy engine ordering.
Sam: Two quick experiments: 1) switch to pinned memory + cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated copy stream, 2) push NVTX ranges around submit to see CPU call timing.
Alex: Tried pinned + async copy on a separate stream but still saw occasional 10-40ms gaps. I profiled with osrt and saw the host thread blocked on an internal mutex during batching commit.
Priya: That internal mutex could come from our batching heuristic updating shared batch state. If submission is serialized behind that lock, even async memcpy won't help much.
Sam: Right — the overlap requires: allocate pinned, cudaMemcpyAsync(h2d, ..., copy_stream), cudaEventRecord(copy_done, copy_stream), cudaStreamWaitEvent(compute_stream, copy_done) then kernel launch. Also ensure the host thread posts memcpy work and returns quickly (no sync).
Alex: Patch I tried: replaced sync memcpy with\n```\ncudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, copy_stream);\ncudaEventRecord(evt, copy_stream);\ncudaStreamWaitEvent(compute_stream, evt);\n// submit kernel immediately after scheduling copy\nlaunch_kernel(compute_stream, ...);\n```\nJonah: That should let copy engine and kernels overlap. But still need to remove any `cudaStreamSynchronize` or implicit syncs in our helper wrappers.
Sam: For debugging, add NVTX push/pop around the batching lock and submission. Then re-run nsys with `--trace=osrt,cuda,nvtx` to correlate host lock hold times with gaps in CUDA submissions.
Alex: Did that. New trace shows much smaller idle periods. The big gaps were ~25ms -> now tail spikes are ~3-5ms. Device occupancy improved and memcpy timelines overlap with kernels more.
perf-bot: build/trace report uploaded: s3://redwood-profiles/1779990012_kvprefetch_nsystar.zip
Priya: Nice. Next steps: 1) make prefetch use pinned pools (recycler) 2) move submission off critical path (submit queue + worker thread) 3) avoid any sync calls in the hot path 4) add NVTX instrumentation for critical runtime ops.
Sam: Also check kernel selection: smaller kernel variants were chosen earlier because of short sequence length estimate — that causes many short kernels with higher per-kernel overhead. Consider grouping tokens into larger batches or force a bigger-kernel path for throughput-critical flows.
Alex: Agreed. I'll open a PR with pinned buffer pool + submission worker. Will attach a before/after nsys timeline in the PR.
Priya: One caution — pinned memory hurts page-fault heavy code and increases commit charge. Use bounded pool and reuse.
Jonah: And verify on dedicated machines where copy engine concurrency differs (older GPUs have single copy engine). Put a flag to fallback to sync-copy for single-CE devices.
Alex: Thanks all — will post results here when PR lands. :thumbsup:
Sam: Great work. Short-term perf win, long-term we should add a small synthetic test to detect submission jitter in CI.
Alex: Yep — adding a nightly perf job with an nsys trace for regression detection.
Priya: Perfect. :rocket:
